title: Landform classification with the Topographic Position Index
text: Topographic Position Index (TPI) compares elevation cell digital terrain model (DTM) mean elevation cells around (Guisan et al. 1999; Weiss 2001). Positive values mean cell higher surroundings (ridge hilltop), negative values lower (valley bottom), values near zero either flat ground half-way slope; slope used tell two apart. landform implements two classifications proposed Weiss (2001) made popular Jenness’s TPI extension ArcView (Jenness 2006): Slope Position Classification, six classes one TPI scale; Landform Classification, ten classes small large TPI scale. package three functions: landform(), performs classifications; tpi(), returns TPI surface ; malta_dtm(), loads sample DTM used .

title: Landform classification with the Topographic Position Index
text: DTM covers island Malta 40 m resolution, sea coded NA.
code: library(landform) library(terra) #> terra 1.9.50  dem <- malta_dtm() dem #> class       : SpatRaster #> size        : 535, 580, 1  (nrow, ncol, nlyr) #> resolution  : 40, 40  (x, y) #> extent      : 438651.4, 461851.4, 3962750, 3984150  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) #> coord. ref. : ED50 / UTM zone 33N (EPSG:23033) #> source      : malta_dtm_40.tif #> name        : elevation plot(dem, col = hcl.colors(50, "Terrain 2"), main = "Malta DTM (m)")

title: Landform classification with the Topographic Position Index
text: Weiss’s thresholds expressed standard deviations, TPI standardised first. Two approaches available, can lead noticeably different maps. Global (std = "global", default). TPI turned z-scores using mean standard deviation TPI whole raster. method Weiss (2001) Jenness (2006): value 1 means “one standard deviation typical TPI landscape”. Local (std = "local"). TPI cell divided standard deviation elevation neighbourhood, “deviation mean elevation” (DEV) Wilson Gallant (2000). De Reu et al. (2013) found better suited landscapes relief varies greatly place place. drawback nearly flat areas local standard deviation tiny, small irregularities DTM (plain noise) become large standardised values. method available landform version 0.2. difference easiest see plateaus plains eastern Malta:  local standardisation flat areas broken mosaic valleys ridges cells across. method preferable depends landscape question; doubt, worth running .
code: g <- landform(dem, scale = 9, plot = FALSE) l <- landform(dem, scale = 9, std = "local", plot = FALSE) par(mfrow = c(1, 2)) plot(g$classes, main = "Global standardisation", legend = FALSE,      mar = c(1, 1, 2, 1), axes = FALSE) plot(l$classes, main = "Local standardisation", legend = FALSE,      mar = c(1, 1, 2, 1), axes = FALSE) par(mfrow = c(1, 1)) data.frame(class = g$stats$class,            global = round(g$stats$percent, 1),            local = round(l$stats$percent, 1)) #>          class global local #> 1       Valley    7.7   3.2 #> 2  Lower Slope    8.3  11.7 #> 3   Flat Slope   48.7  43.0 #> 4 Middle Slope   13.3  24.4 #> 5  Upper Slope   12.2  14.3 #> 6        Ridge    9.7   3.4

title: landform 0.3.0
text: landform() now returns object class "landform" print(), summary() plot() methods, holding classes single categorical SpatRaster (classes, class names colours), TPI slope layers, descriptive statistics (always computed; now also mean elevation slope per class), input DTM settings. list per-class rasters returned earlier versions (result$, result$Valley, …) replaced result$classes class_layers(result); result[["Descriptive Statistics"]] replaced result$stats (summary(result)). Class names now follow Jenness (2006) (e.g. “Midslope Ridges, Small Hills Plains” instead “Midslopes Ridges-Small Hills Plains”).

title: landform 0.3.0
text: New colour palettes: ordinal blue--brown palette Slope Position Classification, hues grouped landform family Landform Classification (replace rainbow()). Custom colours via col. legend placed outside map default, data hidden (leg.pos still accepts usual keywords). Optional relief shading underneath classes TPI: slopeshade (shade = "slope", slope grey levels white flat terrain black steepest slopes) hillshade (shade = "hill"), overlying layer drawn semi-transparently (alpha). bar plot class areas horizontal labelled class names. plot(x, = "tpi") maps standardised TPI surface(s). plot = FALSE suppresses plotting.
